punch_items.evidence: Done-when: 'Consolidate solvers behind one dispatcher... with identical results and metadata... backend agreement is asserted on the same networks.' tools/pcb_trace_resistance.py's _solve_dense, solve_cg, _solve_scipy, HAVE_SCIPY, DENSE_NODE_LIMIT, calibrate_solver, estimate_seconds are now literally pathminer.core.solver's objects (is-identity asserted in tests/test_compatibility.py::test_facade_solver_primitives_are_the_pathminer_core_objects). network_resistance (the one dispatcher every call site in this file already used) now builds an edge list and delegates the solve to pathminer.core.solver.two_terminal_resistance, forcing the same dense/sparse crossover it always used (test_network_resistance_routes_through_two_terminal_resistance, which spies on the call). Backend agreement through this route demonstrated on the same network both ways (test_network_resistance_dense_and_sparse_backends_agree, V11 unbalanced-bridge vector forced through dense and sparse via dense_limit=1). Full V-vector set re-verified end to end: --selftest 118/118 headless and 284/284 on the real IP5385 board, both matching the frozen golden fixtures exactly.

Done-when: 'module tests and the aggregate --selftest report the same acceptance-vector identities.' Session 04 already retained V11/V13/V14/V20 identities in tests/test_solver.py/tests/test_geometry.py. tests/test_compatibility.py::test_aggregate_selftest_reports_the_module_split_vector_identities checks this as an EXACT identity match (strengthened in coordinator-review repair; the first cut only checked a shared name prefix, which a reviewer correctly flagged as too weak to catch a renamed/removed vector): the aggregate --selftest's V11/V13/V14 names, all passing, are compared set-for-set against the module tests' own identities (V11 imported directly from tests/test_solver.py's V11_CASES, so a rename there is caught automatically; V13/V14 hand-transcribed from that file's and tests/test_geometry.py's inline comments and documented as such, since neither keeps those identities in an importable structure), computed through the same pathminer.core.solver/geometry objects the module tests exercise directly. V20's backend-agreement check is gated on a board fixture (a '/SDA' net) not present in this repository's fixtures and is documented as pre-existing 'skipped' in tests/baseline/README.md for both canonical suites; explicitly excluded and explained in the test, not silently ignored (see known_issues).

Done-when: 'Add tools/build_single_file.py after the package split. Done when: the generated file passes the same aggregate self-test as the package.' tools/build_single_file.py added: generate_source() locates the facade's pathminer.core bootstrap by sentinel comments and replaces it with pathminer/core/geometry.py and pathminer/core/solver.py inlined into throwaway module objects, so the generated file has no import-time dependency on pathminer at all (test_generated_single_file_has_no_pathminer_package_dependency; also manually verified by running the generated file from /tmp with a minimal env). --check regenerates the file and diffs its --selftest vector-by-vector against the split facade's: 118/118 both headless; 284/284 both with --board against the real IP5385 board. Coordinator review found and reproduced a real bug: check() could report a false PASS when both sides' --selftest failed identically (e.g. both '0/1 checks passed', exit 1), because it only compared the two runs against each other and never confirmed either had actually passed. Fixed: each side is now validated independently (exit 0, parseable summary, passed==total, no FAIL vector) before any comparison; a missing/unparseable summary now fails cleanly instead of raising TypeError. Three regression tests pin the fix. This evidence entry reflects the corrected, no-longer-falsifiable check().

tests.command: Manual repro of the reviewer's false-PASS finding: patch.object(build_single_file, '_run_selftest', return_value=<fake CompletedProcess: returncode=1, stdout='...0/1 checks passed'>), then check(None)
tests.result: Before the fix: returned 0 and printed PASS (bug reproduced exactly as reported). After the fix: returns 1 with a FAIL diagnostic naming both sides' own failure. Permanently pinned by test_check_does_not_pass_when_both_sides_fail_identically.

decisions: Aliases (name = _pm_solver.name / _pm_geometry.name), not wrappers, wherever the v0.13 signature already matched the pathminer.core one exactly, so is-identity can be asserted directly as proof of one shared dispatcher rather than trusting a numeric coincidence.

network_resistance keeps its own r<=0 pre-filter and explicit dense/sparse crossover computed from len(adj) vs dense_limit (the same test this function has always used), then delegates only the actual linear solve to pathminer.core.solver.two_terminal_resistance with an explicit backend= override - not left to that function's own 'auto', which counts nodes from the post-filter edge list and could pick a different crossover point on a graph with dropped edges.

The pathminer.core bootstrap in tools/pcb_trace_resistance.py is delimited by explicit sentinel comments (PATHMINER_CORE_BOOTSTRAP_BEGIN/END), not AST slicing or a fixed line range, so tools/build_single_file.py can find and replace exactly the right block regardless of unrelated edits elsewhere, and fails loudly (RuntimeError) if the sentinels are ever missing or renamed.

Inlined pathminer.core modules become throwaway types.ModuleType objects bound to the existing _pm_geometry/_pm_solver names (not `from x import *`), so every downstream call site in the facade works unchanged in the generated single file.

tools/build_single_file.py --check compares parsed [PASS]/[FAIL] <name> identity and totals, not raw got/want text, because a few vectors (V19, V23) legitimately print a fresh tempfile.mkdtemp() path on every run - the same reason tests/baseline/regression_compare.py normalizes those fields before comparing against a frozen golden fixture.

network_resistance's stricter failure behavior on invalid input (a named ValueError for a disconnected/invalid network, inherited from pathminer.core.solver's already-reviewed _prepare validation) was accepted, not defended against, after the full regression run showed it unchanged before/after and a new failure-path test (test_network_resistance_raises_on_a_disconnected_graph) confirmed the new behavior; no acceptance vector or real-board path exercises the previously inconsistent behavior with a valid answer.
